questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was very interested in the research outputs of the department of geography as I wanted to do fieldwork for my thesis in Oaxaca using collabotive cartography as a methodology.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The administrative paperwork was quite intensive and I struggled quite a bit with that. Other than this, it was a great experience and I could learn a lot!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not very easy because my host institution only emailed us in July about it so it was quite stressful to get all the information last minute and buy the plane tickets on time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Very little, there was one information meeting but it didnt help me much. I had to figure things out by myself, and i had quite some issues registering for courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used facebook and that worked quite well. I would recommend students to live in the centre of Coyoacan since its a very lovely area not to far from uni by both bike and bus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You should definetly try to live close to campus since distances in Mexico City are huge. However, be careful where you choose to live because some areas close to the CU campus are not that safe at night.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was invited to an information meeting where they explained how to register for courses. However, we didnt get much information about the facilities of the university, the extracurricular activities that we could join or life on campus.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the posgraduate exchange office but they are not very responsive

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It took me a really long time because they hadn't registered me properly in the system. I finally managed to get it fixed after visiting various offices.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was a very messy process and the administration (for masters students at least) is not the most responsive. I would recommend you to go in person to their office, it is easier to communicate with them that way.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was taking master courses from geography

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes were very small (3-4 students) which allowed for more in-class discussions and for a closer relationship with the professors. However, I feel that it was more theoretical than at KU:

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Natural Protected Areas, Political Geography and Global Mobilities in Comparative Perspective

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Political Geography - it was quite theoretical but the professor was amazing
Global Mobilities in Comparative Perspective - lots of good reading and practical resources, although quite centered in Europe

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Medical expenses that were uncovered by my insurance

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some supermarkets were more expesive than others. Going out to coffee places or to party could also be quite expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a huge range of sports clubs, language school, artistic activities, student associations, expositions, museums, etc. I highly recommend it

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Climbing, there is a lovely community and they offer good quality trainings. They also have great dance and music shows that you can attend at a very cheap price.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Oaxaca is a beautiful place to visit if you have the time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy as I come from a similar culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speaking the language and joining some non-academic activities. It is quite easy to make new friends everywhere you go

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The perception of time

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The literature, museums, music shows, and food from different regions. Its a culturally rich country and you will enjoy it a lot!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try as many off-school activities as possible with fellow students, be patient with the administration and visit the mountains.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The learning opportunities at UNAM both from professors and classmates. I also enjoyed learning about their culture and art.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The UNAM administration

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
